terms.gloss: a tray or small trough: the tray at a security check
terms.comment: Classically a small hollow vessel, “a tray, trough, basin” (Lewis & Short), the diminutive of alveus; its use for the tray one’s things go through the scanner in is modern, and ours. Traupman and Morgan–Owens have a tray only for serving food, ferculum (Traupman 73) and repositōrium (M-O s.v. dish: tray).
A wooden box or a woven basket for keeping money, clothes, books or fruit (Lewis & Short), applied by us to the tray at the security check, which is shallower than a box.

phrases.latin: Pēram in cistam posuit, lapidem, cum rogārētur, prōmpsit
phrases.english: He put his bag in the tray and, when asked, took out the stone
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum
